description:
FILED s470bv (Opus, 2026-09-06).  A BOOKKEEPING task, deliberately: "pre-existing
is WHEN, not WHY" (ruled s421), and these rows were spliced with a WHEN only.

WHAT HAPPENED.  s470bv brought baselines/perl-suite-run.tsv honest for 51 files.
Sixteen of them moved inside the batches merged that day and are attributed to a
COMMIT by measurement (#1115 / #1221 / s470bs #1048).  Two more were bisected
because they are LOSSES (op/multideref.t -> #1058, an accepted divergence;
run/fresh_perl.t -> #1057, task #1273).

THE REMAINING 33 read IDENTICALLY at 614c6af, at 424cabc and on the s470bv tree,
so they are older than the s470 batches -- in several cases much older: the
snapshot values date from the s440 file move (2026-08-24) or before.  Every one
is a GAIN (PCL got better and nobody told the snapshot).  They were spliced with
the note "stale at 614c6af, before the s470 batches; NOT bisected -- see task
#1276".  The list:

    comp/parser.t      50/48 -> 51/47
    io/perlio.t        22/0  DIFF -> 46/2 OK
    io/perlio_open.t    0/0  DIFF ->  9/1
    op/each.t          35/12 -> 37/10
    op/gmagic.t        30/3  -> 31/2
    op/symbolcache.t    4/3  ->  6/1
    op/tiearray.t      36/39 -> 40/35
    op/utfhash.t       91/0  -> 97/0
    and the 25 mro/* files (basic_01..05 x c3/dfs x +-utf8, method_caching,
      next_method +-utf8, next_skip +-utf8, basic_04_c3 +-utf8, vulcan_c3 +-utf8)

THE mro FAMILY, checked and NOT what the s471 ruling assumed.  The ruling said
the cause would be the mro PROVIDER; `git log --oneline -- lib/mro.pm
cl/pcl-mro.lisp` shows lib/mro.pm has not changed since s401c (a licence tag)
and every cl/pcl-mro.lisp commit is an artifact REGENERATION at a generation
bump.  So the mro rows moved because generic method resolution / `->can` got
better, over many sessions, not because the provider changed.  Attributed by
git log, NOT re-run.
Four of the 25 now MATCH perl exactly and their registrations were dropped;
21 keep the registration and had their ROWS re-blessed (41 rows no longer
diverge).  Worth checking when this task is picked up: whether
docs/not-supported.md §mro is still accurate about what PCL cannot do -- three
of its claims (the C3 MRO answers, `can`, the dispatch-path rows) are now
satisfied.  Do NOT edit that section without re-reading the 21 registrations'
remaining rows.

WHY IT IS NOT WORTH BISECTING NOW.  Each row is a GAIN; the cost of a bisect is
~8 companion runs plus a core build per step, times 33; and the count snapshot's
job (catch the NEXT move) is done the moment the row is correct.  What is NOT
acceptable is leaving the debt uncounted, which is what this task is.

WHAT WOULD DISCHARGE IT: either (a) bisect the ones that still matter when a
related area is touched, one at a time, or (b) close it with a note once a full
`--all --jobs 4 --bless-stamps` run has re-measured the whole snapshot and the
project accepts the refreshed values as the new zero.  Option (b) is the cheap
one and belongs to a merge-time full companion run, not to a fix session.
subject: ATTRIBUTION DEBT: 33 companion snapshot rows spliced in s470bv were ALREADY stale at 614c6af (older than the s470 batches) and were spliced WITHOUT a bisect -- the list, so the debt is countable rather than inferred
